disclaimer: Researched and verified June 2026 (IRS sources where noted). Educational only — not legal or tax advice; confirm specifics with a CPA for your state.

feeReality: Local pickup = 0%. Facebook charges no platform fee and no payment fee on local in-person sales — verified mid-2026 across every source checked, including Value Added Resource's coverage of Meta's fee announcements.

Shipped checkout = 10% of the total buyer payment (item + shipping + tax collected), $0.80 minimum per order. Meta DOUBLED this from the historical 5%/$0.40 effective April 15, 2024; rates last verified May 2026 against official Meta Business Help pages (sellerfeecalc). Several 2026 SEO articles still claim 5%/$0.40 — they are stale; 10%/$0.80 is current.
The $0.80 floor means items under $8 shipped effectively pay more than 10%.

Shipped checkout still exists in the US but is fragmented: Meta-provided prepaid shipping labels were discontinued for new listings on Feb 24, 2025 (buy your own via Pirate Ship/USPS; a quiet partial reinstatement for select sellers was reported ~Sept 2025), and access to enabling shipping varies by account — many accounts never see the option.

Separately, Meta phased out native checkout for Facebook/Instagram Shops (business storefronts) June–Aug 2025 — a different product than Marketplace P2P checkout, but it signals Meta's retreat from handling payments.

Practical bottom line: treat FB Marketplace in 2026 as a local-first, cash platform. Route shipped card deals to eBay/TCGplayer, or use PayPal Goods & Services (~3%) in BST groups. For local: cash is standard; Zelle/Venmo/Cash App only if you verify the money landed inside your own app at the meetup; never PayPal Friends & Family.

setupSteps.step: Use an established personal account, not a fresh one
setupSteps.detail: Brand-new accounts frequently hit 'Marketplace isn't available to you' or heavy restrictions: roughly 5–10 active listings, posts held for review, and a probation lifting over ~30–90 days (est. — community-reported; Meta publishes no thresholds). New accounts that immediately list high-value items are prime flag/ban candidates. An account with real history is unanimously recommended across seller guides.

setupSteps.step: Build trust signals before listing cards
setupSteps.detail: Complete profile with a real photo, verified phone, 2FA enabled. Sell a few cheap low-risk items first, respond fast (within an hour where possible), and mark items sold promptly.

Marketplace listing is fundamentally a personal-profile feature; native Shops checkout died in 2025. A Page is optional branding only for a card seller — skip it unless building a storefront brand (verified direction, details est.).

setupSteps.step: Join the major Pokemon BST groups — that's where serious card volume happens
setupSteps.detail: Pokemon TCG Buy•Sell•Trade Market (facebook.com/groups/PokemonTCGMarket), Pokémon TCG Sell and Trade (facebook.com/groups/202007151080914), Pokemon Cards Trade, Sell, and Buy (facebook.com/groups/pokemonfb), Pokemon Cards Buy/Sell/Trade supported by Veriswap (facebook.com/groups/169517816782271), PokéMart TCG, plus regional groups. Top groups run 50k–100k+ members (est. — counts not visible logged-out).

Timestamp photos (card + handwritten username/date), price + shipping terms in the post, PWE (~$0.70–1.40, no tracking) vs BMWT (~$4–5, tracked) declared up front, PayPal G&S only, no F&F, no razzes/raffles in most groups, scammer-list checks. Exact rules vary per group.

Work toward Highly Rated / Very Responsive / Top Shipper badges (verified — Facebook Help describes ratings/badges). Ask buyers for ratings after smooth deals. Default search radius buyers see is ~40 miles.

safetyRules: Meet at police safe-exchange zones — hundreds of US departments run camera-monitored 24/7 lots/lobbies (safetradestations.com lists them). Use the lobby for high-value deals, go daytime, bring a friend.
Cash counted on the spot; counterfeit pen for $100s on high-value deals.
Verify any P2P payment (Zelle/Venmo/Cash App) inside YOUR own app before handing over cards — never trust a screenshot or email. Fake payment screenshots are a documented top scam.
There is no 'Zelle business account upgrade' fee — spoofed emails claiming you must be paid extra or refund a difference are a scam (CNBC documented a $500 loss in 2025).
PayPal Goods & Services only for any shipped or non-cash stranger deal; never Friends & Family — no protection, and 'F&F only' is a walk-away red flag.
Never use a buyer-provided shipping label (reroute / claimed non-delivery scam). Payments from stolen Venmo/PayPal accounts get clawed back — another reason for cash on local deals.
Verify graded-slab cert numbers on PSA/CGC/Beckett before the meetup; watch for the meetup switcheroo (card/slab swapped or inspected-and-palmed) — real pattern, prevalence est. (community-reported).
Keep all conversation in Messenger — moving to email/text is a phishing vector. Don't hold items without a deposit.
whatSellsBest: Trading cards are allowed — a dedicated 'Trading Cards' Marketplace category exists (verified). Constraints: no counterfeits, and razzes/raffles/mystery-pack mechanics risk the gambling prohibition (enforcement est.).
FB's sweet spot (verified consensus): bulk lots, commons, sealed product, and high-value local cash deals.
eBay remains better for graded slabs and individual chase singles — largest buyer pool and sold comps; TCGplayer for commodity singles.

Net math: eBay all-in ≈ 13.5–16% effective (13.25% FVF + $0.30–0.40/order + shipping risk); FB local = 0%; FB shipped = 10%/$0.80. FB local asking prices typically run ~10–30% under eBay sold comps (est. — community consensus), so FB local net ≈ eBay net on most items, with FB winning on bulk/lots and time-to-cash.
High-value listings (~$500+) on young accounts may be held for review (est. — community-reported).

urls.prefillNote: Title/description prefill via URL DOES NOT EXIST — confirmed absence; no documented deep-link params in Meta docs or third-party tooling (listing tools like Vendoo/Crosslist use browser-extension DOM automation, not URL prefill). Plan on copy-paste or extension automation. The create URL is login-gated (shows Marketplace landing page logged-out, not a 404); /marketplace/create is the type chooser. Useful search params: daysSinceListed=1, deliveryMethod=local_pickup (verified via scraper docs); sortBy=creation_time_descend, minPrice/maxPrice also work (est. — undocumented but widely observed). Region-scoped pattern: facebook.com/marketplace/<city>/search/?query=...

ten99kNow: Federal 1099-K threshold for 2025 and 2026 is back to $20,000 AND more than 200 transactions — the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed July 4, 2025) retroactively repealed the ARPA $600 phase-in. IRS confirmed via FAQs and Fact Sheet FS-2025-08 (Oct 23, 2025). The scheduled $5,000/$2,500/$600 steps are dead. (Verified, primary IRS sources.)

Several STATES keep their own lower thresholds and marketplaces must report to them regardless: MA/VT/VA/MD at $600 (any transaction count); IL at over $1,000 + 4+ transactions; others (NJ, DC) have used lower thresholds — confirm your state for the filing year.

The trap: receiving (or not receiving) a 1099-K changes nothing about what you owe. All income is reportable whether or not the form is issued — the higher threshold is less automatic paperwork, not a tax cut.
hobbyVsBusiness: There are THREE possible tax characters for a card/collectibles seller, taxed very differently: (A) selling your own personal collection, (B) hobby, (C) business/dealer.

(A) Personal collection: gains are capital gains — cards/memorabilia are 'collectibles' under IRC §408(m), so long-term gains (>1 yr) are taxed at your ordinary rate CAPPED at 28% (a cap, not a flat rate — below-28% brackets pay their lower rate); short-term gains are ordinary. Losses on personal-use property are NOT deductible (investment-documented items may get capital-loss treatment — fact-specific).

(B) Hobby is the worst of both worlds: report 100% of gross income (Schedule 1, line 8j) with ZERO expense deductions for 2018–2025 (TCJA suspended the old hobby-expense deduction) — taxed on gross with no cost-of-cards offset.

(C) Business: net profit on Schedule C at your ordinary rate PLUS ~15.3% self-employment tax — but you deduct COGS, grading/authentication fees (PSA/BGS/CGC), shipping & supplies, platform/payment fees, mileage, home office, software, show tables.

The hobby/business line is IRC §183's nine-factor test (businesslike books, profit motive, time/effort, expertise...), with a safe-harbor presumption of 'for profit' if you show a profit in 3 of the last 5 years.
Key insight: for an active reseller, Schedule C business treatment usually BEATS hobby treatment even with SE tax — the SE tax is the price of being allowed to deduct COGS and expenses.
COGS timing: you generally deduct a card's cost in the year it SELLS, not the year you buy it — a $2,000 box bought in December is not a December write-off if unsold.
llcEconomics: A single-member LLC is a 'disregarded entity': ZERO federal income-tax difference vs. a sole proprietorship — same Schedule C, same rates, same ~15.3% SE tax. An LLC by itself saves you no federal tax.
What it buys is a liability shield (house/savings vs. business lawsuits/debts) — and only if you maintain separation (separate bank account, no commingling), or a court can pierce the veil.

Costs (verified 2026 ranges): one-time state filing ~$35–$500 (US average ~$132; Montana $35, Kentucky $40, many states $50); annual report $0–$300; registered agent $0 if yourself, $50–$300/yr for a service.

California flag: $800 minimum annual franchise tax every year, due even at a loss, plus a gross-receipts fee once CA income tops $250k. For a small CA reseller, $800/yr can exceed the entire liability benefit.

S-corp election is the only move that actually cuts SE tax (salary + distributions split) — rule of thumb is it starts paying off around $50k–$80k+ of consistent net profit (est. — practitioner consensus), because it adds ~$1.5k–$3k/yr in payroll/bookkeeping/tax-prep and requires a defensible reasonable salary.

Insurance caveat: a personal umbrella policy typically EXCLUDES business/commercial activity — it is not a substitute. A genuine business wants commercial liability (a Business Owners Policy) and possibly inventory/shipping coverage.

decisionTiers.tier: Tier 1 — Casual: under ~$5k/yr revenue, or just liquidating your own collection
decisionTiers.advice: No LLC — its cost outweighs any benefit here. Likely hobby or personal capital-asset treatment: report gains (collectibles LTCG capped at 28%), losses on personal items non-deductible, hobby expenses non-deductible. Keep a simple cost-basis record so you only pay tax on actual gains. No EIN or permit needed; marketplaces handle sales tax.

decisionTiers.tier: Tier 2 — Side business: ~$5k–$30k/yr, buying to flip regularly
decisionTiers.advice: File Schedule C as a sole proprietor: income tax + ~15.3% SE tax on net, but you now deduct COGS, grading, shipping, fees, mileage, home office — usually better than hobby status. Get the free EIN + separate bank account + resale certificate; keep per-item COGS books. LLC = optional: worth it mainly in a cheap-filing state, with high-value consignment/inventory, or if you want the separation — weigh hard in California ($800/yr minimum). Consider commercial liability insurance instead of or alongside it.

Operate as a real business; an LLC now makes sense for liability (shows, high-dollar shipments, helpers) plus clean banking/credit identity. Carry commercial liability + inventory insurance; pay quarterly estimated taxes; consider a CPA. Watch the $600 state 1099-K triggers (MA/VA/MD/VT) if you operate there.

Run the S-corp election math (LLC taxed as S-corp) to cut SE tax via the salary/distribution split — only with a defensible reasonable salary and a bookkeeper/CPA, since it adds ~$1.5k–$3k/yr in compliance (threshold est. — practitioner consensus). Below ~$50k net it usually costs more than it saves.

setupChecklist.step: Get a free EIN directly from IRS.gov
setupChecklist.detail: Free; avoid third-party sites that charge. Useful even as a sole proprietor so you don't hand out your SSN on resale certificates.

setupChecklist.step: Open a separate business bank account
setupChecklist.detail: The single most important habit — it's what makes you 'businesslike' under §183 AND what preserves an LLC's veil if you ever form one.

setupChecklist.step: Get a resale certificate / state sales-tax permit
setupChecklist.detail: Issued by your state (distinct from the EIN). Lets you buy inventory tax-free for resale; required if you ever collect tax yourself.

Purchase price, date, grading fee, sale price, fees, shipping — makes COGS defensible and is your §183 'businesslike records' evidence. A spreadsheet or tool (MyResellerGenie, Hurdlr) is enough at small scale. Remember: COGS is deducted in the year the item sells, not when bought.

setupChecklist.step: Know who handles sales tax where
setupChecklist.detail: Marketplace-facilitator laws mean eBay/Amazon/Etsy/Mercari/Whatnot collect and remit sales tax FOR you in all sales-tax states. FB shipped orders through Meta checkout: Meta is responsible. FB LOCAL cash/Venmo/Zelle sales: Facebook collects nothing — a true reseller flipping inventory locally is the one technically on the hook for applicable sales tax.
A personal umbrella policy typically excludes business activity — for a genuine reselling operation use commercial liability (Business Owners Policy) and possibly inventory/shipping coverage.

llc.verdict: Skip the LLC for now — at this scale it buys nothing and costs real money. A single-member LLC is a federally disregarded entity: identical Schedule C, identical ~15.3% SE tax, zero federal tax savings. Its only product is a liability shield costing ~$35–$500 to form (US average ~$132) plus $0–$300/yr in annual report fees and up to $300/yr for a registered agent — and a flat $800/yr minimum franchise tax in California even at a loss. Liquidating a ~$14k collection plus flipping used games and guitars is unlikely to clear the ~$30k/yr-net tier where the shield starts earning its keep, and the 1099-K reversion to $20k + 200 transactions (IRS-verified for 2025/2026) means no automatic paperwork at this volume anyway — though every dollar of real profit is still taxable, and MA/VT/VA/MD trigger reporting at $600. The actual money move at this tier is electing business (Schedule C) treatment so COGS, grading, shipping, platform fees, and mileage are deductible instead of being taxed on gross as a hobby — the SE tax is the price of those deductions. The one line that changes the LLC calculus is the 3D-print rigs: that's a NEW manufactured product designed and shipped to strangers, the kind of real liability exposure the research flags as the legitimate LLC trigger — flipping used cards and games is not. If the rig line gets real traction (roughly $10k+/yr revenue or meaningful assembled-unit volume — threshold est.), form the LLC around that brand in a cheap-filing state and pair it with a commercial BOP, since a personal umbrella excludes business activity. Hold any S-corp election until ~$50k–$80k consistent net profit (est.) — below that, the $1.5k–$3k/yr in compliance eats the SE-tax savings. Until then: free EIN + separate bank account + resale certificate + per-item COGS books + commercial liability insurance delivers ~90% of the LLC's practical benefit at a fraction of the cost. Not legal or tax advice — confirm state specifics before acting.

venueMatrix.bestVenues: eBay (graded slabs, premium/chase singles) · FB Marketplace local (bulk, lots, sealed, high-value cash) · TCGplayer (commodity singles)
venueMatrix.fees: eBay 13.25–13.6% FVF + $0.40/order (12.7% with Basic Store, $21.95/mo annual); FB local 0%; FB shipped 10%/$0.80 min; eBay runs recurring 50%-off FVF promos on $1,000+ card singles
venueMatrix.note: FB local asks run ~10–30% under eBay sold comps (est.), so FB-local net ≈ eBay net on most items — FB wins on bulk/lots and time-to-cash, eBay wins on buyer pool, comps, and Authenticity Guarantee. Verify 13.25 vs 13.6% per-category in Seller Hub (sources conflict).

venueMatrix.bestVenues: eBay (shippable games) · FB Marketplace local (consoles, lots, local cash)
venueMatrix.fees: eBay ~13.25–13.6% + $0.40/order (12.7% with Basic Store); FB local 0%; FB shipped 10%/$0.80 min
venueMatrix.note: FB shipped checkout at 10% is no longer cheap — use FB for local/lot sales only and route shippable games to eBay. FVF conflict (13.25 vs 13.6%): verify in Seller Hub before pricing.

venueMatrix.bestVenues: eBay Guitars & Basses (lowest fee for shippable) · Reverb (gear-buyer intent) · FB local (amps, cabs, heavy gear — no fee, no shipping risk)
venueMatrix.fees: eBay Guitars & Basses 6.35% FVF (5.85% with Basic Store+) + $0.40/order (est. — sources conflict, one claimed 12% capped $350; check the live fee table); Reverb 5% (cap $500) + 3.19% + $0.49 processing ≈ 8.2% all-in (Preferred: 2.99% + $0.49); FB local 0%
venueMatrix.note: On a $1,000 guitar: eBay ≈ $64, Reverb ≈ $82, FB local $0. Reverb is independent again — Etsy's sale to Creator Partners LLC + Servco Pacific (Fender's majority owner) closed June 2, 2025; no fee hikes announced under new ownership as of June 2026.

venueMatrix.bestVenues: Etsy (primary launch venue) · eBay (secondary channel) · Shopify deferred until owned traffic justifies it
venueMatrix.fees: Etsy: $0.20 listing + 6.5% transaction + 3% + $0.25 processing + one-time $15 shop setup ≈ 10–12.5% all-in typical (Offsite Ads 15% opt-out under $10k / 12% mandatory over, capped $100/order); eBay ~13.6%, no originality rule; Shopify Starter $5/mo + 5% transaction ≈ 8%+/sale, Basic $39/mo ($29 annual) + 2.9% + $0.30
venueMatrix.note: Etsy's Creativity Standards (updated June 10, 2025) require 3D-printed items be the seller's ORIGINAL design — third-party/licensed STL prints are out. Brandon designs his own rigs, so he's squarely allowed and the rule purges licensed-STL competitors from search. Sell the three-tier ladder: STL → kit + hardware pack → assembled rig.

venueMatrix.bestVenues: MakerWorld Exclusive (points + BOM commissions) or Gumroad (direct sales) + an Etsy digital listing · Printables Store secondary
venueMatrix.fees: Gumroad 10% + $0.50/transaction direct (30% on Discover sales), no monthly fee; MakerWorld Exclusive $0.066/Exclusive Point as of May 2026 (cash out at $100+, exclusivity required) + NEW 3–15% cash commission when buyers order BOM parts/kits from your model page (effective Mar 24, 2026); Printables Store 20% fee + Stripe (net ~60–75%, $5 min price); Etsy digital = same fees as physical, .stl supported, 5 files x 20MB
venueMatrix.note: Keep the flagship rig STL paid/exclusive; post a free teaser or accessory model for funnel traffic — giving the flagship away undercuts paid kit sales. The MakerWorld BOM commission is directly relevant to a rig with screws/inserts hardware. Etsy digital files also fall under the original-design rule.

accountStrategy: ONE established eBay account for all used lines (cards, games, non-guitar gear) — feedback history is the asset and used-goods buyers don't care about catalog coherence. eBay explicitly allows multiple accounts (policy id=4232, 'separate accounts for different product lines'), but feedback doesn't transfer, new accounts start at zero with low selling limits, and a suspension on one can restrict the others. Only split if the 3D-print line gets big enough to want its own storefront branding.

Add an eBay Basic Store ($21.95/mo annual): pays for itself vs 13.6% non-store rates at roughly >$2.5k/yr in discounted categories; 1,000 free fixed-price listings/mo. (Starter at $4.95/mo has NO FVF discount.)

Facebook: keep using the personal profile for local sales — business Pages cannot use the simple 'create listing' flow (Commerce Manager/Shop catalog only). A business Page per brand is only worth it for the 3D-print brand as a marketing surface (posts, groups, ads), not as a Marketplace selling vehicle.

Etsy: ONE shop, 3D-print products only, named for the product brand. Multiple shops are allowed but each needs its own account/email, public disclosure of your other shops, no duplicate listings, and $15 setup each. Used games/cards don't belong on Etsy at all (handmade / 20-yr-vintage / craft-supply rules), and a mixed shop converts worse in Etsy's relevance-driven search.
printBrand: Yes — a distinct brand/shop for the rig line is worth it; it's the standard playbook for successful functional-print sellers, and niche focus (card imaging) outperforms generalist print shops.

Three-tier laddering: STL-only (~$12–25, ~95% margin, infinite stock) → printed kit + hardware pack (mid price, buyer assembles, cheap to ship) → fully assembled/calibrated rig (premium, 2–3x kit). Top sellers run all three simultaneously.
License tiers on the STL: personal / small-commercial / unlimited-commercial at rising prices.

Bundle a card-photography setup guide PDF (lighting, white balance, PSA/eBay photo standards) with every tier — near-zero cost, big differentiation, and it cross-sells the actual card listings as proof of results.
Design an ecosystem/series: accessories (phone mounts, light diffusers, slab holders, toploader jigs) that lock buyers into the system.
MakerWorld's BOM commissions (3–15%, Mar 2026) enable a hybrid play: paid/exclusive flagship STL + kit listing there, while Etsy carries the assembled/kit physical tiers.

Name caution: a 'DarkHearts'-style brand fits (matching Etsy/Gumroad/MakerWorld profiles, same logo on inserts), but check the name reads as photography-gear-friendly to strangers — the shop name is the search-result trust signal.
crossPromo: Core rule everywhere: platforms only police diverting an in-progress sale off-platform — not post-purchase or external marketing.

eBay: the 'offers to buy or sell outside eBay' policy (id=4272) bans offsite links/contact info in LISTINGS and eBay MESSAGES. Physical package inserts are allowed. Safe play: a card in every shipped Pokemon/game order — 'I also make the rig this card was photographed with' + brand URL/QR + social handles. Never put the URL in listings or messages.

Etsy: fee-avoidance policy bans completing Etsy-originated sales off-platform and offsite links in listings/Messages; inserts are fine and customary. Bonus: Etsy Share & Save — share your own tracked shop link (socials, email, business cards, inserts) and Etsy refunds the equivalent of 4% of attributed orders; Etsy actively rewards the insert/social funnel toward Etsy.
Reverb: same pattern — keep listings clean, inserts fine (est. — policy page not directly fetched; consistent with marketplace norms).

Legal flow that works everywhere: every shipment (cards, games, gear) carries the 3D-print brand insert; every STL/guide download contains links to all storefronts; social accounts (the YouTube 'Ansom' channels are an obvious engine) link to everything.
